tasks.note: The sweep's failure (all 116 files at startup: "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'config')", "Vitest failed to find the runner") was worker startup, not this feature's code; the user ruled that vitest.config.mts belongs to the other session running on this feature, so I left it alone. What I did fix, on the user's call, is a real race the sweep's config change exposed: test/repo-map-files.test.ts's a_reader_during_a_build_sees_a_whole_file_never_a_partly_written_one re-read a 400 KB file with no gap, so a handle was open ~99% of the time and Windows refused the build's rename onto it (EPERM) until the retry budget ran out - it failed about three runs in five on its own. The reader now lets go for 25ms between reads, as a session that reads the map once does, and the test still proves a reader never sees half a file. 6/6 green on that file, the whole suite green (1416 passed, 3 skipped), npm run typecheck clean. (src/agent/workspace-files.ts's longer, backing-off retry budget came from the other session, not from me.)

SdkSession.buildOptions (src/agent/sdk-session/sdk-session.ts) now always sets settings: { autoMemoryEnabled: false }.

tasks.note: Empirically verified (real `claude -p` runs against a throwaway CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, not just the .d.ts) that under this codebase's actual wiring (`settingSources: ['project','local']`, `autoMemoryEnabled: false`, both pre-existing and untouched here) the Claude engine reads neither scope natively today, so "no second copy" has nothing to dedupe on the Claude side; both scopes are added there explicitly, the same words the own loop's instruction-file read already says for the person's notes. On the own loop, only the user scope was already covered (by the pre-existing, unrelated "instruction files" feature reading ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md whole); the project scope was not reaching it at all before this task, on either engine, in any mode.
tasks.built: `src/agent/memory/session-context.ts`: wantsMemories(mode) = mode !== 'plan'; MemorySources = {project, user}; readMemorySources(cwd, home) reads the project's MEMORY.md and the person's whole `## Memories` section (via memories.ts's new userMemorySection); memorySection(sources) renders both into one "## What is already known" block, index-only (a project note's body is never inlined, only its index line), and states "the project note holds" on a clash, but only when both scopes have notes; withMemories(mode, systemPrompt, cwd, home) appends that block for every mode but 'plan', used as `ctx.withMemories` (new field on ModeContext, wired in mode-setup.ts's implement/code-plan/docs/file-decisions/docs-map/reconcile/cleanup cases, deliberately left out of 'plan'); chatMemorySection(cwd, home) = memorySection(readMemorySources(...)) reused by session-engines.ts's startClaude for its chat/full-access branch (both scopes, since the Claude engine's own CLAUDE.md loading excludes `user` and its auto-memory tool is off). memories.ts gained userMemorySection(text). system-prompt.ts's buildSystemPrompt (the own loop's chat prompt) now also appends the project index alongside the instruction files it already reads whole (which is where the person's own notes already reach it, so only `project` is passed there, not `user`, avoiding a second copy on that engine's side too).

tasks.note: The sweep's suite-wide failure ("Vitest failed to find the runner", "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'config')" on all 123 files, before any test ran) is the test runner on Windows, not this feature's code: from a working directory spelled with a lower-case drive letter (`d:\...`, how the harness and some shells spell it) Vitest resolves itself under two spellings of the same path and loads itself twice. Reproduced exactly by running `npm test` from `d:\...` (123 failed, no tests). The earlier attempt to normalize the drive letter from inside vitest.config.mts does not work - also tried with an explicit `root` - because by the time the config is loaded the double resolution has happened; the fix is now `scripts/run-tests.mjs`, which `npm test` runs: it normalizes the drive letter and spawns Vitest as a child process that only ever sees the upper-case spelling. vitest.config.mts keeps pool: 'threads' (per-file isolation without a 120+ process spawn storm) and now only documents the requirement. Verified: `npm test` from `d:\...` green (120 passed, 3 skipped, 1597 tests), from `D:\...` green, narrowed runs (test/memories.test.ts, test/settings-app.test.ts: 58 passed) green, `npm run typecheck` clean.
tasks.built: Test runner entry: `npm test` now runs `scripts/run-tests.mjs`, which upper-cases the working directory's drive letter and spawns `node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run` with the remaining arguments forwarded, so `npm test -- <file> -t "<name>"` still narrows a run. vitest.config.mts keeps pool: 'threads' and the markdown-as-text plugin; it no longer chdirs (too late to help). Unchanged otherwise: memories.ts (listMemories, forgetMemory, removeUserMemoryBullet, memoryPath), settings-store.ts MemoryPort/SettingsStore.forgetMemory, SettingsSnapshot.memories, FromSettingsWebview open_memory/forget_memory, settings-panel.ts memoryPathOf, the webview Memories tab (memories-tab.ts, MemoryOpenedEvent/MemoryForgottenEvent).
